constraints.meaning: The array can be empty and has at most 100 elements.
constraints.impact: Even O(n²) is only 10⁴ steps, so brute force passes. One pass, O(n), is still the clean answer. The code must return 0 for an empty array.
No overflow risk: int is enough in every language.

constraints.meaning: val can be bigger than any value in nums.
constraints.impact: val may not appear at all. Then nothing is removed and the answer is nums.length.

constraints.meaning: You may not build a second array.
constraints.impact: O(1) extra space. This rules out 'copy the kept values into a new array' and points to two pointers inside one array.

constraints.text: Only the first k elements count, in any order (statement)
constraints.meaning: The judge sorts nums[0..k-1] before it checks them, and ignores everything after index k-1.
constraints.impact: You never need to clean up the tail, and you may overwrite values freely. Copying each kept value forward is enough.

bruteForce.summary: each time you find val, shift everything after it one step left: O(n²) time, O(1) space. Copying the kept values into a new array is O(n) time, but it needs O(n) extra space, which breaks the in-place rule.
